overview.title: Time a short GPT training loop
overview.summary: A stripped training loop that reports step time and a rough utilization for a 12-layer GPT.

sections.title: Bench a few steps of a GPT-2 sized model
sections.pseudocode:
Use batch 12, context 1024, 12 layers, 12 heads, and width 768.
Run configurator.py, then either memory-map real tokens or draw random ids below 50304.
Step AdamW at learning rate 1e-4 and weight decay 1e-2, with moments 0.9 and 0.95.
Optionally profile 5 plus 5 plus 5 steps and write a trace to bench_log.
Seed from 1337. Otherwise burn in for 10 steps, time 20, and print milliseconds times 1000 and percent times 100.
# Insight: Nothing is saved. The point is the clock.

logic.title: Time a short GPT training loop
logic.summary: Run a few forward and backward steps on a 12-layer GPT and report milliseconds and estimated utilization.

sections.title: Fixed bench settings
sections.pseudocode:
Use batch 12 and context 1024.
Leave bias off, and read real data unless told otherwise.
Seed from 1337.
Run on cuda, in bfloat16 when the GPU supports it, else float16.
Compile the model.
Skip the profiler unless profile is set.
Run configurator.py, which executes overrides.
Allow tf32, and use autocast on cuda.
# Insight: This file is a shorter train.py. It does not save checkpoints or decay the learning rate.

sections.title: Real tokens, or a random stand-in
sections.pseudocode:
If real data is on, memory-map OpenWebText train.bin.
Draw windows of **block_size** and the following ids, and move them to the device.
Otherwise fill the batch with random ids below 50304.
Reuse that same random batch every step.
# Why: Random ids remove the disk read, so the timing is closer to pure model math.

sections.title: Build a 12-layer GPT and an AdamW
sections.pseudocode:
Use 12 layers, 12 heads, and width 768.
Turn dropout off, which is 0, so the timing does not jitter.
Build the GPT and move it to the device.
Use AdamW with weight decay 1e-2, learning rate 1e-4, and moments 0.9 and 0.95.
Compile when asked.

sections.title: Optional profiler trace
sections.pseudocode:
Wait 5 steps, warm up for 5, then record 5.
Profile CPU and CUDA, and write a trace under bench_log.
For each of those steps, score a batch, fetch another, zero gradients, go backward, and step.
Print the step and the loss.
Tell the profiler the step finished.
# Insight: The trace is for the PyTorch profiler UI. The simple loop below is the one that prints utilization.

sections.title: Time a burn-in, then a measured loop
sections.pseudocode:
Synchronize cuda so the clock starts clean.
First run 10 steps and ignore their time. Then run 20.
Each step scores, prefetches, zeros gradients, goes backward, and steps.
Print the loss.
Synchronize again and estimate utilization.
On the measured stage, print milliseconds, times 1000, and the percent, times 100.
# Why: The first 10 steps pay for compile and caches. The next 20 are the number the print trusts.
